title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光
title.en: Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第十一 魏舒 李憙 劉寔 高光 Volume 41 Biographies 11: Wei Shu; Li Xi; Liu Shi; Gao Guang

sentences.zh: 魏舒，字陽元，任城樊人也。

translations.literal: Wei Shu, styled Yangyuan, was a man of Fan in Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu, courtesy name Yangyuan, was a native of Fan in Rencheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為外家寧氏所養。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was raised by his mother's family, the Ning clan.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father while still a boy and was brought up by his maternal kin, the Ning family.

sentences.zh: 寧氏起宅，相宅者云：「當出貴甥。

translations.literal: When the Ning built a house, the geomancer said: "There will emerge a noble nephew."
translations.idiomatic: When the Nings built a residence, a geomancer said: "This house will yield an eminent nephew."

sentences.zh: 」外祖母以魏氏甥小而慧，意謂應之。

translations.literal: Continuing (after the prophecy), his maternal grandmother, taking the Wei nephew to be small yet clever, thought it referred to him.
translations.idiomatic: His maternal grandmother assumed the prophecy meant her clever little Wei grandson.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「當為外氏成此宅相。

translations.literal: Shu said: "It shall be for the maternal clan that this house fulfills its auspicious site."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu said: "It will be my mother's family for whom this lucky layout comes true."

sentences.zh: 」久乃別居。

translations.literal: Continuing the account, only after a long time did he live apart.
translations.idiomatic: Only much later did he move out and live separately.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺二寸，姿望秀偉，飲酒石餘，而遲鈍質樸，不為鄉親所重。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi two cun in height; his bearing was handsome and imposing; he drank more than a shi of wine; yet he was slow, dull, and plain, and was not esteemed by his townsfolk.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi two cun tall, with a striking presence, and could drink more than a shi of wine at a sitting; yet he seemed slow and unpolished, so neighbors did not think much of him.

sentences.zh: 從叔父吏部郎衡，有名當世，亦不之知，使守水碓，每歎曰：「舒堪數百戶長，我願畢矣！

translations.literal: His father's cousin Heng, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, had renown in the age, yet did not recognize him either, and made him guard the water mill, sighing each time: "Shu suffices for the head of several hundred households—my wish is fulfilled!"
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Heng, a Personnel Bureau director celebrated in their day, still failed to appreciate him and left him tending the water mill, sighing: "Wei Shu is enough for a headman over a few hundred households—that satisfies me."

sentences.zh: 」舒亦不以介意。

translations.literal: Continuing, Shu likewise did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu did not resent it.

sentences.zh: 不修常人之節，不為皎曆之事，每欲容才長物，終不顯人之短。

translations.literal: He did not cultivate ordinary men's propriety; he did not perform dazzling deeds; he always wished to accommodate talent and foster things, and in the end never exposed others' shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: He did not fuss over ordinary propriety or seek flashy accomplishments; he preferred to make room for others' abilities and strengths, and never aired their faults.

sentences.zh: 性好騎射，著韋衣。

translations.literal: By nature he loved riding and archery and wore leather garments.
translations.idiomatic: He loved riding and shooting and dressed in leather hunting clothes.

sentences.zh: 入山澤，以漁獵為事。

translations.literal: He entered mountains and marshes and took fishing and hunting as his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his time fishing and hunting in the hills and wetlands.

sentences.zh: 唯太原王乂謂舒曰：「卿終當為台輔，然今未能令妻子免饑寒，吾當助卿營之。

translations.literal: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan said to Shu: "You will in the end become a pillar minister; yet now you cannot enable wife and children to escape hunger and cold—I shall help you provide for them."
translations.idiomatic: Only Wang Yi of Taiyuan told him: "You are destined for the highest offices, but right now you cannot keep your family from want—I will help you set yourself up."

sentences.zh: 」常振其匱乏，舒受而不辭。

translations.literal: Continuing, he often relieved his poverty; Shu accepted without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi repeatedly eased his straits, and Wei Shu accepted without refusing.

sentences.zh: 舒嘗詣野王，主人妻夜產，俄而聞車馬之聲，相問曰：「男也，女也？

translations.literal: Shu once went to Yewang; the host's wife gave birth at night; presently they heard the sound of carriages and horses, and asked one another: "Male or female?"
translations.idiomatic: Once when Wei Shu visited Yewang, the host's wife went into labor at night; soon voices outside sounded like horses and carriages, asking: "Is it a boy or a girl?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「男，書之，十五以兵死。

translations.literal: The reply continued: "Male; record it—at fifteen he will die by weapons."
translations.idiomatic: The reply came: "A boy—note this: he will die by arms at fifteen."

sentences.zh: 」復問：「寢者為誰？

translations.literal: They asked again: "Who is the sleeper?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again: "Who is sleeping here?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「魏公舒。

translations.literal: The answer continued: "Lord Wei Shu."
translations.idiomatic: The answer was: "Wei Shu."

sentences.zh: 」後十五載，詣主人，問所生兒何在，曰：「因條桑為斧傷而死。

translations.literal: Fifteen years later he went to the host and asked where the child born then was; it was said: "Because while pruning mulberry he was wounded by an axe and died."
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen years later Wei Shu called on the host and asked after that child; he was told the boy had died when an axe cut him while he was stripping mulberry branches.

sentences.zh: 」舒自知當為公矣。

translations.literal: Continuing, Shu himself knew he would become a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu understood then that he would rise to ducal rank.

sentences.zh: 年四十餘，郡上計掾察孝廉。

translations.literal: When he was over forty, as clerk for the commandery accounts mission he was nominated Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty, he served as the commandery clerk on the annual accounting mission and was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 宗党以舒無學業，勸令不就，可以為高耳。

translations.literal: Clansmen and kin, because Shu had no scholarly accomplishment, urged him not to take office, so as to be esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: His clansmen, noting he had little formal learning, urged him to decline the nomination and preserve a reputation for lofty refusal.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「若試而不中，其負在我，安可虛竊不就之高以為己榮乎！

translations.literal: Shu said: "If I try and am not selected, the fault is mine—how can I vainly steal the esteem of not going for my own glory!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu replied: "If I sit the examination and fail, the blame is mine; I must not borrow fake 'high-minded' refusal just to polish my name."

sentences.zh: 」於是自課。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set himself a curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: So he drilled himself.

sentences.zh: 百日習一經，因而對策升第。

translations.literal: In a hundred days he studied one classic; thereby he answered policy questions and rose in rank.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered one classic every hundred days, passed the policy examination, and advanced.

sentences.zh: 除澠池長，遷浚儀令，入為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Mianchi, promoted to magistrate of Junyi, and entered as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was named magistrate of Mianchi, then of Junyi, and eventually entered court as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 時欲沙汰郎官。

translations.literal: At that time they wished to weed out Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court then planned to purge underperforming palace gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 非其才者罷之。

translations.literal: Those not of talent were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone judged inadequate would be removed.

sentences.zh: 舒曰：「吾即其人也。

translations.literal: Shu said: "I am precisely such a person."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu said: "That describes me."

sentences.zh: 」襆被而出。

translations.literal: Bundling his bedding, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He packed his bedding and walked out.

sentences.zh: 同僚素無清論者咸有愧色，談者稱之。

translations.literal: Colleagues who ordinarily had no pure reputations all showed shame; discussers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Coworkers who lacked sterling reputations were ashamed; commentators praised him.

sentences.zh: 累遷後將軍鐘毓長史，毓每與參佐射，舒常為畫籌而已。

translations.literal: He was promoted repeatedly to chief clerk to Rear General Zhong Yu; whenever Yu shot with his aides, Shu always merely kept score with tallies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk under Rear General Zhong Yu; when Zhong practiced archery with his staff, Wei Shu usually only kept score.

sentences.zh: 後遇朋人不足，以舒滿數。

translations.literal: Later when companions were insufficient, they used Shu to fill the quota.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when there were not enough partners for the round, they added Wei Shu to make up the party.

sentences.zh: 毓初不知其善射。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not know he was skilled at shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu had not realized he could shoot.

sentences.zh: 舒容范閒雅，發無不中，舉坐愕然。

translations.literal: Shu's bearing was leisurely and elegant; his releases all hit; the whole assembly was stunned.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu carried himself with calm elegance and never missed; everyone at the table sat dumbstruck.

sentences.zh: 莫有敵者。

translations.literal: There was none who matched him.
translations.idiomatic: No one could beat him.

sentences.zh: 毓歎而謝曰：「吾之不足以盡卿才，有如此射矣，豈一事哉！

translations.literal: Yu sighed and apologized, saying: "My inadequacy to exhaust your talent is like this shooting—is it only one matter!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Yu sighed and said: "If I failed to use your abilities fully in archery, how much more elsewhere?"

sentences.zh: 」轉相國參軍，封劇陽子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to aide to the minister of state and enfeoffed as Baron of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as aide to the minister of state and enfeoffed as Baron of Ju.

sentences.zh: 府朝碎務，未嘗見是非；

translations.literal: In the bureau's petty affairs he never showed right or wrong;
translations.idiomatic: In routine office trivia he never picked fights;

sentences.zh: 至於廢興大事，眾人莫能斷者，舒徐為籌之，多出眾議之表。

translations.literal: as for great matters of abolishing or promoting, where the multitude could not decide, Shu slowly deliberated them and often produced conclusions beyond the crowd's deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: but on weighty questions of state where others could not decide, he thought them through calmly and often surpassed every other proposal.

sentences.zh: 文帝深器重之，每朝會坐罷，目送之曰：「魏舒堂堂，人之領袖也。

translations.literal: Prince Wen deeply esteemed him; whenever court assembly seating ended, following him with his gaze he said: "Wei Shu is imposing—the people's leader."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen of Wei valued him highly; after each court session he watched him leave and said: "Wei Shu has true presence—he is born to lead men."

sentences.zh: 」遷宜陽、滎陽二郡太守，甚有聲稱。

translations.literal: He was promoted governor of the two commanderies Yiyang and Xingyang and had great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He became governor of Yiyang and Xingyang and earned wide acclaim.

sentences.zh: 徵拜散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and named Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 出為冀州刺史，在州三年，以簡惠稱。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Ji Province; in the province three years, he was praised for simplicity and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He served three years as Inspector of Ji Province and was noted for straightforward, humane rule.

sentences.zh: 入為侍中。

translations.literal: He entered as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝以舒清素，特賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu, because Shu was pure and plain, specially granted one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his austerity and gave him a special gift of one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，以公事當免官，詔以贖論。

translations.literal: He was promoted Master of Writing; because of official business he ought to have been dismissed; an edict ruled ransom.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Master of Writing; a bureaucratic fault should have cost him his post, but an edict allowed him to commute the penalty.

sentences.zh: 舒三娶妻皆亡，是歲自表乞假還本郡葬妻，詔賜葬地一頃，錢五十萬。

translations.literal: Shu thrice took wives and all died; that year he memorialized asking leave to return to his native commandery to bury his wives; an edict granted burial land one qing and five hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: All three of Wei Shu's wives had died; that year he asked leave to return home and bury them, and the throne granted one qing of burial ground and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 太康初，拜右僕射。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taikang he was appointed Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taikang era he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 舒與衛瓘、山濤、張華等以六合混一，宜用古典封禪東嶽，前後累陳其事，帝謙讓不許。

translations.literal: Shu with Wei Guan, Shan Tao, Zhang Hua, and others, because the six directions were unified, held that the classical rite of feng and shan should be performed on the Eastern Marchmount; before and after they repeatedly presented this matter; the emperor modestly declined and did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu joined Wei Guan, Shan Tao, and Zhang Hua in arguing that, with the realm reunited, the classical Eastern Peak feng and shan sacrifices should be held; they petitioned repeatedly, but the emperor modestly refused.

sentences.zh: 以舒為左僕射，領吏部。

translations.literal: Shu was made Left Vice Director and supervised the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and oversaw the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 舒上言：「今選六宮，聘以玉帛，而舊使禦府丞奉聘，宣成嘉禮，贄重使輕。

translations.literal: Shu submitted: "Now in selecting the six palaces, betrothal uses jade and silk; yet by old practice the imperial treasury assistant conducts the betrothal and proclaims and completes the auspicious rites—the gifts are weighty but the envoy is light.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu memorialized: "When filling the six palaces we send jade and silk as bride-price, yet we still send the imperial treasury assistant to deliver it—the ceremony is grand but the envoy too lowly."

sentences.zh: 以為拜三夫人宜使卿，九嬪使五官中郎將，美人、良人使謁者，於典制為弘。

translations.literal: It is held that investing the Three Ladies ought to employ a minister; the Nine Concubines ought to employ a commander of household gentlemen for all purposes; the Beauties and Good Women ought to employ heralds—thus with statutory ritual it is magnified.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that investitures for the Three Ladies use a minister, for the Nine Concubines a commander of household gentlemen for all purposes, and for Beauties and Good Women court heralds—better fitting the statutes."

sentences.zh: 」有詔詳之，眾議異同，遂寢。

translations.literal: An edict ordered detailed deliberation; the multitude's opinions differed; thereupon it was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered discussion, but opinions conflicted and the reform stalled.

sentences.zh: 加右光祿大夫、儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was added Right Household Grandee with ceremonial parity of the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally named Right Household Grandee with privileges matching the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 及山濤薨，以舒領司徒，有頃即真。

translations.literal: When Shan Tao died, Shu was placed in charge of the Minister of Education; shortly thereafter he held it substantively.
translations.idiomatic: After Shan Tao died, Wei Shu headed the Ministry of Education ad interim and soon received the full appointment.

sentences.zh: 舒有威重德望，祿賜散之九族，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Shu had awe-inspiring weight and virtuous renown; stipends and gifts he scattered to the nine kindreds; the household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu commanded respect; he shared stipends and gifts across his extended clan and kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 陳留周震累為諸府所辟，辟書既下，公輒喪亡，僉號震為殺公掾，莫有辟者。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu was repeatedly summoned by various bureaus; once the summons went down, the lord always died; all called Zhen the clerk who killed lords; none summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhen of Chenliu had been invited by several offices, but each patron died as soon as his appointment arrived; people called Zhou the "official-killer" and no one would hire him.

sentences.zh: 舒乃命之，而竟無患，識者以此稱其達命。

translations.literal: Shu thereupon ordered him, and in the end there was no trouble; those who understood praised this as understanding fate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu hired him anyway, and nothing happened; observers praised his grasp of destiny.

sentences.zh: 以年老，每稱疾遜位。

translations.literal: Because of old age, he often claimed illness and yielded position.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing in years, he repeatedly pleaded illness to resign.

sentences.zh: 中復暫起，署兗州中正，尋又稱疾。

translations.literal: In the meantime he briefly rose, was appointed provincial evaluator of Yan Province, and presently again claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: He briefly returned to serve as provincial evaluator for Yan Province, then again pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞郤詵與舒書曰：「公久疾小差，視事是也，唯上所念。

translations.literal: Left aide to the Masters of Writing Xi Shen wrote to Shu: "Your lordship's long illness has slightly improved—attending to affairs is right; only what superiors ponder."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shen, Left Aide to the Masters of Writing, wrote: "You have been ill but are a little better—returning to duty is appropriate; that is what the court expects."

sentences.zh: 何竟起訖還臥，曲身回法，甚失具瞻之望。

translations.literal: How can you in the end rise and then return to bed, bending the body and twisting the law—greatly losing the hope of the one on whom all gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Why get up only to go back to bed, bending rules to suit yourself? You disappoint everyone who looks to you.

sentences.zh: 公少立巍巍，一旦棄之，可不惜哉！

translations.literal: Your lordship from youth established towering stature; to abandon it in one morning—is it not regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: You built an eminent reputation long ago; to throw it away now would be a shame!

sentences.zh: 」舒稱疾如初。

translations.literal: Continuing, Shu claimed illness as before.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu again pleaded illness as before.

sentences.zh: 後以災異遜位，帝不聽。

translations.literal: Later because of disasters and prodigies he yielded position; the emperor did not heed.
translations.idiomatic: He later cited omens and resigned; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 後因正旦朝罷還第，表送章綬。

translations.literal: Later on New Year's Day court ending he returned to his mansion and memorialized returning seals and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: After New Year's court he went home and formally returned his seals of office.

sentences.zh: 帝手詔敦勉。

translations.literal: The emperor personally edicted earnest encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with a handwritten note urging him to stay.

sentences.zh: 而舒執意彌固，乃下詔曰：「司徒、劇陽子舒，體道弘粹，思量經遠，忠肅居正，在公盡規。

translations.literal: Yet Shu held his intent ever firmer; thereupon an edict went down: "The Minister of Education, Baron of Ju Shu, embodies the Way broadly and purely; his thought considers what is distant; loyal and solemn he occupies correctness; in public affairs he exhausts counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu remained adamant, so the throne issued an edict: "Minister of Education Wei Shu, Baron of Ju, embodies the Way with breadth and purity; he thinks far ahead; he is loyal, grave, and upright; he gives honest counsel in office.

sentences.zh: 入管銓衡，官人允敘；

translations.literal: Within he manages evaluation and ranking; officials are duly ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Within the ministries he ranks candidates fairly;

sentences.zh: 出贊袞職，敷弘五教。

translations.literal: without he assists the duke's office and spreads the Five Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: as minister he advances the Five Teachings among the people.

sentences.zh: 惠訓播流，德聲茂著，可謂朝之俊乂者也。

translations.literal: Kind instruction spreads abroad; virtuous fame flourishes manifestly—he may be called an eminent stalwart of the court.
translations.idiomatic: His humane counsel spreads wide and his moral renown shines—he is truly one of the court's foremost pillars.

sentences.zh: 而屢執沖讓，辭旨懇誠，申覽反覆，省用憮然。

translations.literal: Yet repeatedly he upholds yielding modesty; his phrases are earnest and sincere; extending perusal turns repeatedly—on examining it I am sorrowful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he insistently asks to step down; his words are heartfelt and sincere. Each time I read his petitions my heart sinks.

sentences.zh: 蓋成人之美，先典所與，難違至情。

translations.literal: Surely completing others' excellence is what former canons grant—hard to oppose utmost feeling.
translations.idiomatic: The classics urge us to honor another's good intentions; I cannot ignore his deepest wishes.

sentences.zh: 今聽其所執，以劇陽子就第，位同三司，祿賜如前。

translations.literal: Now we heed what he holds to; let the Baron of Ju go to his mansion; rank matches the Three Dukes; stipends and gifts as before.
translations.idiomatic: We grant his request: the Baron of Ju may retire home with rank equal to the Three Dukes and the same salary and gifts as before.

sentences.zh: 几杖不朝，賜錢百萬，床帳簟褥自副。

translations.literal: With stool and staff not attending court; granted one million cash; bed curtains and bamboo mat bedding supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He need not attend court; he receives one million cash, plus bedding, curtains, and mats.

sentences.zh: 以舍人四人為劇陽子舍人，置官騎十人。

translations.literal: Four gentlemen attendants are taken as Baron of Ju gentlemen attendants; establish ten official riders.
translations.idiomatic: Four gentlemen attendants will serve his household, with ten official mounted escorts.

sentences.zh: 使光祿勳奉策，主者詳案典禮，令皆如舊制。

translations.literal: Cause the Superintendent of the Household to present the patent; those in charge scrutinize according to ritual statutes; orders all as old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: The Superintendent of the Household shall deliver the patent; officials shall verify everything against precedent.

sentences.zh: 」於是賜安車駟馬，門施行馬。

translations.literal: Thereupon grant secure carriage and four horses; at the gate erect mounting racks.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a comfortable carriage and team and permission to mount barrier poles at his gate.

sentences.zh: 舒為事必先行而後言，遜位之際，莫有知者。

translations.literal: Shu in conducting affairs always acted first and spoke after; at the juncture of yielding position none knew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu always acted before he spoke; when he resigned, nobody had seen it coming.

sentences.zh: 時論以為晉興以來，三公能辭榮善終者，未之有也。

translations.literal: Opinion of the time held that since Jin's rise, among the Three Dukes able to decline glory and end well, there had been none.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said that since the Jin founding no Three Duke had ever relinquished honor so gracefully and died at peace.

sentences.zh: 司空衛瓘與舒書曰：「每與足下共論此事，日日未果，可謂瞻之在前，忽焉在後矣。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Wei Guan wrote to Shu: "Whenever together with you we discussed this matter, day after day it was not realized—it may be called 'before one's eyes, suddenly behind.'"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan, Minister of Works, wrote: "We spoke of this again and again yet never resolved it—the goal seemed within reach, then slipped away."

sentences.zh: 」太熙元年薨，時年八十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taixi he died; at the time age eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first Taixi year at eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 帝甚傷悼，賵賻優厚，諡曰康。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly mourned; burial gifts were generous; posthumous title said Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply; funeral subsidies were lavish; his posthumous name was Kang ("Peaceful").

sentences.zh: 子混，字延廣，清惠有才行，為太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Hun, styled Yanguang, was pure and kind with talent and conduct; he was crown prince attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei Hun, courtesy name Yanguang, was gentle and talented and served as attendant to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，先舒卒，朝野咸為舒悲惜。

translations.literal: At age twenty-seven, before Shu he died; court and countryside all for Shu felt sorrow and pity.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty-seven, predeceasing his father; officials and commoners alike grieved for Wei Shu.

sentences.zh: 舒每哀慟，退而歎曰：「吾不及莊生遠矣，豈以無益自損乎！

translations.literal: Shu often mourned bitterly; withdrawing he sighed: "I fall far short of Master Zhuang—how could I harm myself with what brings no benefit!"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu mourned deeply, then sighed: "I am nowhere near Zhuangzi—why wound myself over what cannot help?"

sentences.zh: 」於是終服不復哭。

translations.literal: Thereupon after mourning ended he did not weep again.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period ended he did not weep again.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「舒惟一子，薄命短折。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Shu has only one son; mean fate, brief broken life.
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Wei Shu had but one son, and fate cut him off young."

sentences.zh: 舒告老之年，處窮獨之苦，每念怛然，為之嗟悼。

translations.literal: In the years Shu announces old age, dwelling in the bitterness of poverty and solitude—each time pondering he is distressed; for it one sighs and mourns.
translations.idiomatic: In his retirement Wei Shu endures loneliness and loss; each thought pains us, and we mourn with him.

sentences.zh: 思所以散愁養氣，可更增滋味品物。

translations.literal: Thinking thereby to dispel sorrow and nurture qi, one may further increase flavors and kinds of goods.
translations.idiomatic: We should find ways to lift his spirits and care for his health—send richer foods and delicacies.

sentences.zh: 仍給賜陽燧四望繐窗戶皁輪車牛一乘，庶出入觀望，或足散憂也。

translations.literal: Further grant and give a yang-sui four-view gauze-window black-wheeled carriage ox team one pair—perhaps going out and looking about may suffice to scatter sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: Also grant him a sun-mirror carriage with four-view gauze windows, black wheels, and a pair of oxen, so outings might ease his sorrow.

sentences.zh: 」以庶孫融嗣。

translations.literal: By the grandson by a concubine Rong he was succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Rong (born of a concubine's line) inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 又早卒，從孫晃嗣。

translations.literal: Again he died early; the grand-nephew Huang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Rong also died young; the heir became his cousin once removed, Huang.

sentences.zh: 李憙，字季和，上黨銅鞮人也。

translations.literal: Li Xi, styled Jihe, was a man of Tongdi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi, courtesy name Jihe, was a native of Tongdi in Shangdang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父牷，漢大鴻臚。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Han Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Quan had served as Grand Herald under the Han.

sentences.zh: 憙少有高行，博學研精，與北海管甯以賢良征，不行。

translations.literal: Xi from youth had lofty conduct; broadly learned he investigated essentials; with Guan Ning of Beihai by Worthy and Good he was summoned; he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi showed sterling character early; he studied widely and deeply. He and Guan Ning of Beihai were summoned as Worthy and Good candidates, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 累辟三府，不就。

translations.literal: Repeatedly summoned by three bureaus, he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Several high offices summoned him; he refused each time.

sentences.zh: 宣帝復辟憙為太傅屬，固辭疾，郡縣扶輿上道，時憙母疾篤，乃竊逾泫氏城而徒還，遂遭母喪，論者嘉其志節。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan again summoned Xi as subordinate to the Grand Tutor; he firmly declined citing illness; commandery and county raised him in a litter onto the road; at that time Xi's mother was gravely ill; thereupon he secretly crossed Xuanshi city wall and walked back; then suffered mother's mourning; discussers praised his resolve and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan summoned him as an aide to the Grand Tutor; he pleaded illness. Local officials carried him toward the capital in a litter, but his mother lay dying, so he slipped away over the wall at Xuanshi and walked home. She died soon after, and observers praised his devotion.

sentences.zh: 後為并州別駕，時驍騎將軍秦朗過并州，州將畢軌敬焉。

translations.literal: Later he became aide for Bing Province; at that time General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang passed through Bing Province; the provincial commander Bi Gui treated him with respect.
translations.idiomatic: He became Bing Province aide; when General of Agile Cavalry Qin Lang traveled through the region, provincial commander Bi Gui showed him full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 令乘車至閣。

translations.literal: He ordered riding in a carriage to the gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gui had him ride in a carriage up to the gate pavilion.

sentences.zh: 憙固諫以為不可，軌不得已從之。

translations.literal: Xi firmly remonstrated that it could not be done; Gui having no choice complied with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi insistently objected; Bi Gui had no choice but to yield.

sentences.zh: 景帝輔政，命憙為大將軍從事中郎，憙到，引見，謂憙曰：「昔先公辟君而君不應，今孤命君而君至，何也？

translations.literal: Prince Jing assisted governance and ordered Xi as aide to the Grand General in attendance; when Xi arrived he was granted audience and said to Xi: "Formerly my late lord summoned you and you did not respond; now I order you and you come—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing, assisting with government, named Li Xi aide to the Grand General. At his audience the prince asked: "Once my father summoned you and you stayed away; now I summon you and you appear—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「先君以禮見待，憙得以禮進退。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your late lord treated me with ritual; Xi could advance or withdraw according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi answered: "Your father treated me according to ritual, so I could accept or decline on those terms."

sentences.zh: 明公以法見繩，憙畏法而至。

translations.literal: The enlightened lord binds me with law; Xi fears the law and therefore came.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness measures men by statute; I respected the law and came.

sentences.zh: 」帝甚重之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought highly of him.

sentences.zh: 轉司馬，尋拜右長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to marshal; soon appointed chief clerk on the right.
translations.idiomatic: He became an army marshal and soon chief clerk on the right.

sentences.zh: 從討毌丘儉還，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Guanqiu Jian he returned and was promoted Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Guanqiu Jian he was promoted to Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.

sentences.zh: 當官正色，不憚強禦，百僚震肅焉。

translations.literal: Holding office with stern demeanor, not fearing the powerful—hundred officials trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: He faced duty with a stern air and did not flinch from the mighty; the bureaucracy stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 薦樂安孫璞，亦以道德顯，時人稱為知人。

translations.literal: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an; by virtue and conduct he too became eminent; people of the time called him one who knows men.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Sun Pu of Le'an, who likewise rose on virtue and conduct; contemporaries said Li Xi could judge character.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大司馬，以公事免。

translations.literal: Soon promoted Grand Marshal; dismissed on official business.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand Marshal but later removed over an administrative matter.

sentences.zh: 司馬伷為甯北將軍，鎮鄴，以憙為軍司。

translations.literal: Sima Zhou was General Who Guards the North, garrisoned Ye, and appointed Xi army clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhou served as General Who Guards the North at Ye, he named Li Xi army clerk.

sentences.zh: 頃之，除涼州刺史，加揚威將軍、假節，領護羌校尉，綏禦華夷，甚有聲績。

translations.literal: Shortly he was appointed Inspector of Liangzhou, added General Who Displays Might, credential bearing, concurrently Colonel Protecting the Qiang—pacifying Chinese and barbarians—had great reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became Inspector of Liangzhou with the additional titles General Who Displays Might and credential-bearing Colonel Protecting the Qiang; he kept Chinese and frontier peoples in check with notable success.

sentences.zh: 羌虜犯塞，憙因其隙會，不及啟聞，輒以便宜出軍深入，遂大克獲，以功重免譴，時人比之漢朝馮、甘焉。

translations.literal: Qiang raiders violated the passes; Xi seized the opening, without awaiting memorial notification, on expedient authority sent troops deep in—thereupon greatly conquered and captured—because merit outweighed fault he was spared punishment; people of the time compared him to Feng and Gan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiang raiders breached the frontier, Li Xi exploited the moment without waiting for court approval and struck deep on discretionary authority, scoring a major victory. Merit outweighed his breach of protocol, so he escaped sanction; people compared him to Feng Fengshi and Gan Yanshou of the Han.

sentences.zh: 於是請還，許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he requested return; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to retire from the post and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 居家月餘，拜冀州刺史，累遷司隸校尉。

translations.literal: Dwelling at home over a month, appointed Inspector of Ji Province; promoted repeatedly to Metropolitan Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month at home he became Inspector of Ji Province and eventually Metropolitan Commandant.

sentences.zh: 及魏帝告禪于晉，憙以本官行司徒事，副太尉鄭沖奉策。

translations.literal: When Wei emperor announced abdication to Jin, Xi in his original office acted Minister of Education affairs, assisting Grand Commandant Zheng Chong presenting the patent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei emperor abdicated in favor of Jin, Li Xi handled Minister of Education duties in his current rank and assisted Grand Commandant Zheng Chong in presenting the abdication patent.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，封祁侯。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning, enfeoffed Marquis of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taishi era he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi.

sentences.zh: 憙上言：「故立進令劉友、前尚書山濤、中山王睦、故尚書僕射武陔各占官三更稻田，請免濤、睦等官。

translations.literal: Xi submitted: "Former Establish Advancement Magistrate Liu You, former Master of Writing Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, former Vice Director Wu Ling each occupy official triple-watch rice paddies—request dismissal of Tao, Mu and others from office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi reported that Liu You, former magistrate of Lijin, Shan Tao, Prince Mu of Zhongshan, and the late Vice Director Wu Ling had each seized government rice lands registered for three irrigation shifts; he asked that Shan Tao, the prince, and others be stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 陔已亡，請貶諡。

translations.literal: Ling having died—request demotion of posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ling was dead, so Li Xi asked that his posthumous title be lowered.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「法者，天下取正，不避親貴，然後行耳，吾豈將枉縱其間哉！

translations.literal: An edict said: "Law is what the world takes as rectitude—without avoiding kin and nobles—only then is it enforced—how could I bend and indulge among them!"
translations.idiomatic: The response read: "Law is the standard for all under Heaven; it must reach kin and nobles alike. Do you think I would twist it to spare anyone?"

sentences.zh: 然案此事皆是友所作，侵剝百姓，以繆惑朝士。

translations.literal: Yet examining this matter—all was done by You—encroaching on and stripping the common people, thereby deceiving court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet this affair was Liu You's doing: he seized land from the people and misled officials at court.

sentences.zh: 奸吏乃敢作此，其考竟友以懲邪佞。

translations.literal: Wicked clerks dared do this—investigate You to the end to punish treacherous flattery.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks dared this malfeasance; try Liu You to the full extent to punish deceit.

sentences.zh: 濤等不貳其過者，皆勿有所問。

translations.literal: As for Tao and others who did not share his fault—none shall be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Tao and others who were not accomplices need not be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱'王臣蹇蹇，匪躬之故'。

translations.literal: The Changes says 'the king's ministers arduous—not for their persons' sake.'
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says: "The king's ministers labor in hardship—not for private ends."

sentences.zh: 今憙亢志在公，當官而行，可謂'邦之司直'者矣。

translations.literal: Now Xi rises with intent for the public good, acting as official duty demands—he may be called 'the state's straight recorder.'
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi stands tall for the common good and does his duty—he is truly the "straight man of the state."

sentences.zh: 光武有云：'貴戚且斂手以避二鮑'。

translations.literal: Guangwu said: 'Noble kin folded hands to avoid the two Baos.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu said even imperial in-laws kept their hands folded to stay clear of Bao Yong and Bao De.

sentences.zh: 豈其然乎！

translations.literal: Is it not so!
translations.idiomatic: Was it not exactly so?

sentences.zh: 其申敕群僚，各慎所司，寬宥之恩，不可數遇也。

translations.literal: Extend strict orders to the host of officials—each be cautious in his charge; indulgent grace cannot often be met.
translations.idiomatic: Tell every official again to mind his duties carefully—such leniency cannot be expected often.

sentences.zh: 」憙為二代司隸，朝野稱之。

translations.literal: Xi served as Metropolitan Commandant for two reigns—court and countryside praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi served as Metropolitan Commandant under two reigns and won praise at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 以公事免。

translations.literal: Dismissed on official business.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed over an administrative matter.

sentences.zh: 其年，皇太子立，以憙為太子太傅。

translations.literal: That year the crown prince was established; Xi was made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The same year the heir apparent was installed, Li Xi became his Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 自魏明帝以後，久曠東宮，制度廢闕，官司不具，詹事、左右率、庶子、中舍人諸官並未置，唯置衛率令典兵，二傅並攝眾事。

translations.literal: From Wei Mingdi onward the Eastern Palace long vacant—institutions abandoned and lacking—offices not complete—Household Superintendent, Left and Right Rates, Household sons, Gentlemen attendants—all offices not yet established—only Guard Rate commander commanded troops—both tutors jointly oversaw all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wei Mingdi the heir's residence had stood empty for years; regulations had lapsed and offices were unfilled—no Household Superintendent, Left or Right Guard superintendents, household sons, or inner gentlemen—only a Guard commander led troops while both tutors handled everything else.

sentences.zh: 憙在位累年，訓道盡規。

translations.literal: Xi held office many years—instructing and advising exhaustively.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi held the post for years, instructing the heir and offering thorough counsel.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書僕射，拜特進、光祿大夫，以年老遜位。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Director of Masters of Writing—appointed Exceptional Advance and Household Grandee—yielded office due to old age.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and received Exceptional Advance and Household Grandee titles before yielding office to age.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「光祿大夫、特進李憙，杖德居義，當升台司。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Household Grandee, Exceptional Advance Li Xi—staff of virtue dwelling in righteousness—ought to ascend terrace ministers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Household Grandee and Exceptional Advance Li Xi upholds virtue and righteousness and ought to join the highest ministers.

sentences.zh: 毗亮朕躬，而以年尊致仕。

translations.literal: He aids and illumines Our person—yet because of advanced years retires.
translations.idiomatic: He has aided and enlightened Us, yet advanced years have led him to retire.

sentences.zh: 雖優遊無為，可以頤神，而虛心之望，能不憮然！

translations.literal: Though leisurely ease without action can nourish spirit—yet the expectation of an empty heart—how can one not be sorrowful!
translations.idiomatic: Leisure may nourish him, yet Our hopes for his counsel leave Us deeply regretful!

sentences.zh: 其因光祿之號，改假金紫，置官騎十人，賜錢五十萬，祿賜班禮，一如三司，門施行馬。」

translations.literal: Accordingly by Household Grandee title change to provisional gold and purple—establish ten official riders—grant five hundred thousand cash—stipends and gifts and court ritual—same as Three Dukes—gate erect horse barriers."
translations.idiomatic: Retain his Household Grandee title but confer provisional gold ribbon and purple robe, assign ten mounted attendants, grant five hundred thousand cash, and extend stipends and ceremonial honors equal to the Three Dukes, including barrier poles at his gate."

sentences.zh: 初，憙為僕射時，涼州虜寇邊，憙唱義遣軍討之。

translations.literal: Earlier when Xi was Vice Director, Liangzhou barbarians raided the border; Xi initiated righteousness sending troops to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Xi was Vice Director, tribes raided Liangzhou; he took the lead in proposing a punitive expedition.

sentences.zh: 朝士謂出兵不易，虜未足為患，竟不從之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen said raising troops was not easy—barbarians not enough to be trouble—in the end did not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials argued that campaigning was difficult and the raid no real threat, so his plan was rejected.

sentences.zh: 後虜果大縱逸，涼州覆沒，朝廷深悔焉。

translations.literal: Later barbarians indeed ran rampant widely—Liangzhou overturned and lost—the court deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes later swept the region unchecked and Liangzhou fell; the court bitterly regretted ignoring him.

sentences.zh: 以憙清素貧儉，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: Because Xi was pure, plain, poor and frugal—granted one hundred bolts silk.
translations.idiomatic: Because Li Xi lived plainly and in poverty, he was granted one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 及齊王攸出鎮，憙上疏諫爭，辭甚懇切。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi Sima You went out to command—Xi submitted memorial remonstrating contending—language very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi Sima You left for his assignment, Li Xi submitted an earnest memorial arguing against it.

sentences.zh: 憙自曆仕，雖清非異眾，而家無儲積，親舊故人乃至分衣共食，未嘗私以王官。

translations.literal: Xi through his successive service—though pure without differing from others—yet household had no stores—kin and old friends even shared clothes and food—never privately used royal office.
translations.idiomatic: Across his career Li Xi was honest like many yet kept no savings; relatives and old friends sometimes shared clothes and food, and he never abused imperial appointment for private ends.

sentences.zh: 及卒，追贈太保，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Upon death posthumously gifted Grand Guardian—posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian with the posthumous name Cheng ("Accomplished").

sentences.zh: 子贊嗣。

translations.literal: Son Zan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Zan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少子儉，字仲約，曆左積弩將軍、屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Youngest son Jian styled Zhongyue—served as Left Strongcrossbow General—Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Li Jian, courtesy name Zhongyue, served as Left Strongcrossbow General and Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 儉子弘，字世彥，少有清節，永嘉末，曆給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Jian's son Hong styled Shiyan—from youth had pure integrity—late Yongjia served Successively Household Gentleman at Yellow Gates—Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian's son Li Hong, courtesy name Shiyan, showed integrity young; late in the Yongjia era he served as Household Gentleman at the Yellow Gates and Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 劉寔，字子真，平原高唐人也。

translations.literal: Liu Shi, styled Zizhen, was a man of Gaotang in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi, courtesy name Zizhen, was a native of Gaotang in Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 漢濟北惠王壽之後也，父廣，斥丘令。

translations.literal: He was descendant of Han Prince Hui of Jibei Shou; father Guang—magistrate of Chiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from Prince Hui of Jibei (Liu Shou) under the Han; his father Liu Guang was magistrate of Chiqiu.

sentences.zh: 寔少貧苦，賣牛衣以自給。

translations.literal: Shi from youth was poor and bitter—sold ox-hide cloak to supply himself.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi grew up destitute and sold straw coats for cattle to get by.

sentences.zh: 然好學，手約繩，口誦書，博通古今。

translations.literal: Yet loved learning—hand gripped rope—mouth recited texts—broadly penetrated past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved learning, knotting cords as he studied and reciting aloud until he mastered classical and recent scholarship.

sentences.zh: 清身潔己，行無瑕玷。

translations.literal: Purified body and cleansed self—conduct without blemish.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself scrupulously clean and his conduct blameless.

sentences.zh: 郡察孝廉，州舉秀才，皆不行。

translations.literal: Commandery nominated Filial and Incorrupt—province raised Cultivated Talent—both times did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him Filial and Incorrupt and the province as Cultivated Talent; he declined both.

sentences.zh: 以計吏入洛，調為河南尹丞，遷尚書郎、廷尉正。

translations.literal: As accounting clerk entered Luoyang—transferred assistant to Henan Governor—promoted Gentleman of Masters of Writing—Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Luoyang as an accounting clerk, became assistant to the Henan governor, then Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and director at the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後曆吏部郎，參文帝相國軍事，封循陽子。

translations.literal: Later served Director in Personnel Ministry—joined Prince Wen minister of state military affairs—enfeoffed Baron of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: He later headed the appointments bureau, joined Prince Wen's minister-of-state staff, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Xun.

sentences.zh: 鐘會、鄧艾之伐蜀也，有客問寔曰：「二將其平蜀乎？

translations.literal: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai campaigned against Shu—a guest asked Shi: "Will the two generals pacify Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Hui and Deng Ai invaded Shu, a visitor asked Liu Shi whether the two generals would conquer it.

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「破蜀必矣，而皆不還。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Destroying Shu is certain—yet none will return.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi replied: "They will crush Shu, but neither will come back."

sentences.zh: 」客問其故，笑而不答，竟如其言。

translations.literal: The guest asked the reason—smiled and did not answer—in the end it was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he smiled and gave no answer; events unfolded exactly as he predicted.

sentences.zh: 寔之先見，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Shi's foresight—all was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His prescience was often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 以世多進趣，廉遜道闕，乃著《崇讓論》以矯之。

translations.literal: Because the age much pursued advancement—yielding and modesty lacking—thereupon composed "Treatise Honoring Yielding" to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing people scramble for promotion while modest yielding had vanished, he wrote "Treatise Honoring Yielding" to correct the trend.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text says:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王之化天下，所以貴讓者，欲以出賢才，息爭競也。

translations.literal: Ancient sage kings' transforming the world—the reason they esteemed yielding—was desiring thereby to bring forth worthy talent and rest contention.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient sage kings prized yielding because it drew forth worthy men and stilled rivalry.

sentences.zh: 夫人情莫不欲已之賢也，故勸令讓賢以自明賢也，豈假讓不賢哉！

translations.literal: As for human feeling none does not desire oneself worthy—therefore urge decree yielding worthies to self-manifest worth—how borrow yielding unworthy!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone wishes to be thought worthy, so we urge men to yield posts to worthier candidates and thereby prove their own worth—it is no sham yielding to the unworthy!

sentences.zh: 故讓道興，賢能之人不求而自出矣，至公之舉自立矣，百官之副亦豫具矣。

translations.literal: Therefore yielding Way rises—worthy able persons without seeking emerge of themselves—supremely impartial selections establish themselves—hundred officials' deputies also beforehand provided.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding prevails, able men appear without being sought, the most impartial appointments take care of themselves, and deputy posts are filled in advance.

sentences.zh: 一官缺，擇眾官所讓最多者而用之，審之道也。

translations.literal: One office vacant—select among crowd of officials the one who yielded most and use him—this is the Way of examination.
translations.idiomatic: When a post opens, pick the candidate whom most colleagues recommended through yielding—that is sound policy.

sentences.zh: 在朝之士相讓於上，草廬之人咸皆化之，推賢讓能之風從此生矣。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen mutually yield upward—thatched-hut persons all are transformed thereby—push worthy yield able wind from this arises.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers yield to one another before the throne, common scholars follow suit, and the custom of recommending worthier men begins.

sentences.zh: 為一國所讓，則一國士也；

translations.literal: By one state yielded to—then one state's gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: One whom a whole kingdom yields to is that kingdom's leading gentleman;

sentences.zh: 天下所共推，則天下士也。

translations.literal: What under Heaven jointly pushes—then under Heaven's gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: one whom all under Heaven recommends is the foremost gentleman of the realm.

sentences.zh: 推讓之風行，則賢與不肖灼然殊矣。

translations.literal: Push yield wind practiced—then worthy and unworthy brightly distinct.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding spreads, the worthy and unworthy stand clearly apart.

sentences.zh: 此道之行，在上者無所用其心，因成清議，隨之而已。

translations.literal: This Way's practice—those above have nowhere to use their hearts—thereby forming pure discussion—following it only.
translations.idiomatic: Under this practice rulers need plot little: pure public opinion forms and they need only follow it.

sentences.zh: 故曰，蕩蕩乎堯之為君，莫之能名。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said—vast vast Yao's being lord—none can name it.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: "So vast was Yao as ruler that none could put a name to his deeds."

sentences.zh: 言天下自安矣，不見堯所以化之，故不能名也。

translations.literal: It means under Heaven self at peace—does not see Yao's means of transforming it—therefore cannot name.
translations.idiomatic: It means the realm was tranquil without anyone pointing to how Yao wrought it, so his virtue could not be labeled.

sentences.zh: 又曰，舜禹之有天下而不與焉，無為而化者其舜也歟。

translations.literal: Also says—Shun and Yu having under Heaven yet not participating therein—without action yet transforming—is it not Shun!
translations.idiomatic: It also says Shun and Yu possessed the realm yet acted as if they did not; Shun transformed all by nonassertive rule.

sentences.zh: 賢人相讓于朝，大才之人恆在大官，小人不爭於野，天下無事矣。

translations.literal: Worthy persons mutually yield at court—great talent persons always at great offices—petty persons do not contend in wilds—under Heaven without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When worthies yield to one another at court, great talent fills high office and common folk cease quarreling in the countryside—the realm is untroubled.

sentences.zh: 以賢才化無事，至道興矣。

translations.literal: By worthy talent transforming without affairs—supreme Way rises.
translations.idiomatic: When worthy talent brings effortless peace, the highest Way prevails.

sentences.zh: 已仰其成，復何與焉！

translations.literal: Already relying on its accomplishment—again what participation therein!
translations.idiomatic: The ruler need only rely on their success—what more must he do?

sentences.zh: 故可以歌《南風》之詩，彈五弦之琴也。

translations.literal: Therefore can sing South Wind poem—strum five-string zither.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he could sing the "South Wind" ode and play the five-string lute.

sentences.zh: 成此功者非有他，崇讓之所致耳。

translations.literal: Completing this accomplishment has no other—honoring yielding's causing only.
translations.idiomatic: No other force produced such success—only the elevation of yielding.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，能以禮讓為國，則不難也。

translations.literal: Confucius says—able to use ritual yielding as state—then not difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "Governing a state through ritual deference is no difficult thing."

sentences.zh: 在朝之人不務相讓久矣，天下化之。

translations.literal: Court persons long have not devoted themselves to mutual yielding—under Heaven transformed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials have long ceased yielding to one another, and the realm has followed suit.

sentences.zh: 自魏代以來，登進辟命之士，及在職之吏，臨見受敘，雖自辭不能，終莫肯讓有勝己者。

translations.literal: Since Wei age onward—ascending advancement summoned gentlemen—and incumbent clerks—facing audience receiving rank—though themselves declining inability—in the end none willing to yield to those surpassing self.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wei dynasty, appointed scholars and serving clerics, when summoned and ranked, even when nominally declining always refuse to yield to anyone better qualified.

sentences.zh: 夫推讓之風息，爭競之心生。

translations.literal: As for push yield wind ceasing—contend compete heart arises.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding dies, the scramble for place begins.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰，上興讓則下不爭，明讓不興下必爭也。

translations.literal: Confucius says—above raises yielding then below does not contend—clarifying yielding not rising below must contend.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "When those above honor yielding, those below do not fight; when yielding does not flourish below, they inevitably fight."

sentences.zh: 推讓之道興，則賢能之人日見推舉；

translations.literal: Push yield Way rises—then worthy able persons daily seen pushed forward;
translations.idiomatic: When yielding prevails, worthy men are recommended day by day;

sentences.zh: 爭競之心生，則賢能之人日見謗毀。

translations.literal: Contend compete heart arises—then worthy able persons daily seen slandered destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: when rivalry grows, worthy men face daily slander.

sentences.zh: 夫爭者之欲自先，甚惡能者之先，不能無毀也。

translations.literal: As for contenders' desire self first—greatly hate able persons' first—cannot without slander.
translations.idiomatic: Those who seek priority resent anyone ahead of them and cannot refrain from tearing him down.

sentences.zh: 故孔墨不能免世之謗己，況不及孔墨者乎！

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius Mozi cannot escape age's slandering self—how much less those not reaching Confucius Mozi!
translations.idiomatic: Even Confucius and Mozi could not escape vilification—what hope for lesser men?

sentences.zh: 議者僉然言，世少高名之才，朝廷不有大才之人可以為大官者。

translations.literal: Discussers uniformly say—age lacks high fame talent—court does not have great talent persons able to be great officers.
translations.idiomatic: Critics all complain that the age lacks celebrated talent and the court has no great men fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 山澤人小官吏亦復雲，朝廷之士雖有大官名德，皆不及往時人也。

translations.literal: Mountain marsh persons petty clerks likewise say—court gentlemen though having great office name virtue—all do not match former times persons.
translations.idiomatic: Rustic clerks echo that today's ministers, however titled or reputed, fall short of earlier generations.

sentences.zh: 餘以為此二言皆失之矣。

translations.literal: I consider these two sayings both miss it.
translations.idiomatic: I believe both judgments miss the mark.

sentences.zh: 非時獨乏賢也，時不貴讓。

translations.literal: Not age alone lacks worthies—age does not esteem yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The problem is not missing worthies but failing to honor yielding.

sentences.zh: 一人有先眾之譽，毀必隨之，名不得成使之然也。

translations.literal: One person having precede crowd's praise—slander necessarily follows—name cannot accomplish makes it thus.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone praised ahead of the pack attracts slander; reputations founder for that reason.

sentences.zh: 雖令稷契復存，亦不復能全其名矣。

translations.literal: Though order Ji Xie again exist—also cannot again preserve complete name.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Ji and Xie lived again, they could not keep their names intact.

sentences.zh: 能否混雜，優劣不分，士無素定之價，官職有缺，主選之吏不知所用，但案官次而舉之。

translations.literal: Able unable mixed confused—excellent inferior not divided—gentlemen lack plain-fixed price—official offices have vacancies—masters of selection clerks do not know whom to use—but examine office order and raise them.
translations.idiomatic: Able and incapable blur together; gentlemen lack fixed standing; when posts open, personnel officers pick blindly by seniority.

sentences.zh: 同才之人先用者，非勢家之子，則必為有勢者之所念也。

translations.literal: Same talent persons first used—either not powerful family's sons—or must be what powerful persons attend to.
translations.idiomatic: Among equals the first chosen are either sons of powerful houses or protégés of the mighty.

sentences.zh: 非能獨賢，因其先用之資，而復遷之無已。

translations.literal: Not able alone worthy—because they first use capital—and again promote them without end.
translations.idiomatic: They are not uniquely worthy; once favored they rise without cease.

sentences.zh: 遷之無已，不勝其任之病發矣。

translations.literal: Promoting them without end—cannot bear their duties' sickness manifests.
translations.idiomatic: Endless promotion breeds failures from incompetence.

sentences.zh: 觀在官之人，政績無聞，自非勢家之子，率多因資次而進也。

translations.literal: Observe incumbent persons—administrative traces unheard—if not powerful family's sons—mostly follow capital order and advance.
translations.idiomatic: Look at officials today: few distinguished records; aside from sons of influence most advance by mere seniority.

sentences.zh: 向令天下貴讓，士必由於見讓而後名成，名成而官乃得用之。

translations.literal: Had the realm esteemed yielding, gentlemen would necessarily come from being seen yielded to before name formed; name formed then offices could employ them.
translations.idiomatic: If yielding were honored across the realm, a scholar would first win renown by being publicly endorsed, and only then could office legitimately take him up.

sentences.zh: 諸名行不立之人，在官無政績之稱，讓之者必矣，官無因得而用之也。

translations.literal: Various persons whose reputation does not stand—in office without administrative traces praise—who would yield to them is certain; offices have no cause thereby to employ them.
translations.idiomatic: Men with no standing reputation and no record of achievement would find no sponsors; the government would have no warrant to appoint them.

sentences.zh: 所以見用不息者，由讓道廢，因資用人之有失久矣。

translations.literal: The reason they are seen employed without cease is because yielding Way is abandoned; reliance on seniority in appointments has erred long.
translations.idiomatic: Endless recycling of unfit officials stems from the collapse of yielding and from long reliance on mere seniority.

sentences.zh: 故自漢魏以來，時開大舉，令眾官各舉所知，唯才所任，不限階次，如此者甚數矣。

translations.literal: Therefore from Han and Wei onward, at times opened great recommendations, ordering crowd of officials each to recommend those known—only by talent appoint—not limited by rank order—such cases were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han and Wei, the court often ordered mass recommendations without rank restrictions—purely talent-based—and did so repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 其所舉必有當者，不聞時有擢用，不知何誰最賢故也。

translations.literal: Among those recommended must be fitting ones—yet we do not hear timely promotions used—because we do not know who is most worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must have been fit, yet timely promotions are unheard of because no one can tell who is worthiest.

sentences.zh: 所舉必有不當，而罪不加，不知何誰最不肖也。

translations.literal: Among recommendations must be unfitting ones—yet guilt not applied—because we do not know who is most unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Some nominees must be unsuitable, yet no one is punished because no one can single out the worst.

sentences.zh: 所以不可得知，由當時之人莫肯相推，賢愚之名不別，令其如此。

translations.literal: The reason it cannot be known is because people of the time will not push one another; worthy and foolish names undistinguished—makes it thus.
translations.idiomatic: The confusion persists because contemporaries refuse to recommend others and blur the worthy with the foolish.

sentences.zh: 舉者知在上者察不能審，故敢漫舉而進之。

translations.literal: Recommenders know those above cannot inspect carefully—therefore dare carelessly recommend and advance them.
translations.idiomatic: Recommenders know superiors cannot vet every nominee, so they nominate recklessly.

sentences.zh: 或舉所賢，因及所念，一頓而至，人數猥多，各言所舉者賢，加之高狀，相似如一，難得而分矣。

translations.literal: Some recommend those they esteem—thereby reaching those they favor—in one rush arriving—persons numerous—each says whom he recommends is worthy—adding lofty descriptions—similar as one—hard to divide.
translations.idiomatic: People nominate favorites and pile on florid praise until every résumé sounds alike and distinctions vanish.

sentences.zh: 參錯相亂，真偽同貫，更復由此而甚。

translations.literal: Mixed wrong together—true and false same threaded—moreover again from this becomes extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Truth and falsehood tangle until the mess grows worse.

sentences.zh: 雖舉者不能盡忠之罪，亦由上開聽察之路濫，令其爾也。

translations.literal: Though recommenders have crime of not exhausting loyalty—also because above opens listening-inspecting road recklessly—makes them thus.
translations.idiomatic: Nominees share blame, yet rulers invite abuse by opening indiscriminate channels for scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 昔齊王好聽竽聲，必令三百人合吹而後聽之，廩以數人之俸。

translations.literal: Formerly King of Qi loved hearing yu sounds—must order three hundred persons jointly blow then listen—granary paid several persons' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi loved ensemble yu pipes and listened only when three hundred played together, paying them like several dozen salaries.

sentences.zh: 南郭先生不知吹竽者也，以三百人合吹可以容其不知，因請為王吹竽，虛食數人之俸。

translations.literal: Mr. Nanguo did not know to blow yu—with three hundred jointly blowing could accommodate his not knowing—therefore requested to blow yu for king—emptily eating several persons' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Mr. Nanguo could not play, but hiding in a choir of three hundred hid his ignorance; he drew several salaries for nothing.

sentences.zh: 嗣王覺而改之，難彰先王之過。

translations.literal: Succeeding king realized and reformed it—difficult to display former king's fault.
translations.idiomatic: The next king saw the problem yet spared his father's reputation.

sentences.zh: 乃下令曰：「吾之好聞竽聲有甚于先王，欲一一列而聽之。

translations.literal: Thereupon ordered: "My liking to hear yu sound exceeds former king—wish one by one array and listen.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed: "I love the yu even more than my predecessor and will hear each player solo."

sentences.zh: 」先生于此逃矣。

translations.literal: Mr. Nanguo here fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that Mr. Nanguo fled.

sentences.zh: 推賢之風不立，濫舉之法不改，則南郭先生之徒盈於朝矣。

translations.literal: If push worthy wind not established—reckless recommendation law not changed—then Nanguo gentlemen fill court.
translations.idiomatic: Until recommending worthies matters and sham nominations stop, the court will swarm with Mr. Nanguos.

sentences.zh: 才高守道之士日退，馳走有勢之門日多矣。

translations.literal: Men of high talent guarding Way daily withdraw—those galloping to powerful gates daily many.
translations.idiomatic: Able men withdraw while climbers flock to powerful houses.

sentences.zh: 雖國有典刑，弗能禁矣。

translations.literal: Though state has statutes and punishments—cannot prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes alone cannot stop it.

sentences.zh: 夫讓道不興之弊，非徒賢人在下位，不得時進也，國之良臣荷重任者，亦將以漸受罪退矣。

translations.literal: As for yielding Way not rising's harm—not only worthies in lower ranks cannot advance in time—state's good ministers bearing heavy duties—also will gradually suffer guilt and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding fails, not only do juniors stall; senior ministers themselves suffer reprimands and fall away.

sentences.zh: 何以知其然也？

translations.literal: How know it is so?
translations.idiomatic: How do we know?

sentences.zh: 孔子以為顏氏之子不貳過耳，明非聖人皆有過。

translations.literal: Confucius considered Yan Hui's son not repeat faults—clarifying not sages all have faults.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius praised Yan Hui for not repeating mistakes—proof that even worthies err.

sentences.zh: 寵貴之地欲之者多矣，惡賢能者塞其路，其過而毀之者亦多矣。

translations.literal: Places of favor and nobility—those desiring them many—those hating worthy able block their paths—those past fault and slander them also many.
translations.idiomatic: Coveted posts attract crowds; rivals block able men and seize on any slip to slander them.

sentences.zh: 夫謗毀之生，非徒空設，必因人之微過而甚之者也。

translations.literal: As for slander arising—not merely empty setup—must be because people's slight faults amplify them.
translations.idiomatic: Slander is seldom invented whole cloth—it magnifies small faults.

sentences.zh: 譭謗之言數聞，在上者雖欲弗納，不能不杖所聞，因事之來而微察之也，無以，其驗至矣。

translations.literal: Destructive slander words repeatedly heard—those above though wish not accept—cannot not staff what they hear—because affairs come and slightly inspect—nothing else—the verification arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors pile up; rulers may wish to ignore them yet must note each report and investigate—evidence soon surfaces.

sentences.zh: 得其驗，安得不理其罪。

translations.literal: Obtaining verification—how can not manage their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Once proof appears, crimes must be punished.

sentences.zh: 若知而縱之，王之威日衰，令之不行自此始矣。

translations.literal: If knowing yet indulging them—king's awe daily declines—commands not executed begin here.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers know yet indulge it, royal authority ebbs and orders cease to run.

sentences.zh: 知而皆理之，受罪退者稍多，大臣有不自固之心。

translations.literal: Knowing yet all managing them—those suffering punishment withdraw gradually many—great ministers have hearts not self-firm.
translations.idiomatic: If every charge is prosecuted, dismissed ministers multiply and senior officials lose confidence.

sentences.zh: 夫賢才不進，貴臣日疏，此有國者之深憂也。

translations.literal: When worthy talent does not advance—noble ministers daily estranged—this is ruler's deep worry.
translations.idiomatic: Blocked talent and estranged ministers are a ruler's gravest concern.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：「受祿不讓，至於已斯亡。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Receiving salary not yielding—arrives at self thus perishes."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says: "Those who take emoluments without yielding bring ruin on themselves."

sentences.zh: 」不讓之人憂亡不暇，而望其益國朝，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: Men who do not yield—worry perishing without leisure—and hope they benefit court—not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Men who refuse to yield fret over survival—how can they benefit the state?

sentences.zh: 竊以為改此俗甚易耳。

translations.literal: I humbly consider changing this custom very easy.
translations.idiomatic: Changing this habit would be easy.

sentences.zh: 何以知之？

translations.literal: How know it?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 夫一時在官之人，雖雜有凡猥之才，其中賢明者亦多矣，豈可謂皆不知讓賢為貴邪！

translations.literal: As for moment's officials—though mixed have vulgar petty talents—among them worthy intelligent also many—how can say all do not know yielding worthy as precious!
translations.idiomatic: Today's officials include mediocrities, yet many are wise—they know yielding is honorable.

sentences.zh: 直以其時皆不讓，習以成俗，故遂不為耳。

translations.literal: Straight because that time all did not yielding—custom formed by habit—therefore finally did not do.
translations.idiomatic: They merely follow habit because no one yields anymore.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，皆通表上聞，名之謝章，所由來尚矣。

translations.literal: Ministers first appointed—all submit memorial reporting upward—named gratitude memorial—origin comes long.
translations.idiomatic: New appointees always memorialize the throne—the "gratitude memorial"—an ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 原謝章之本意，欲進賢能以謝國恩也。

translations.literal: Trace gratitude memorial's root intent—desired advancing worthy able to thank state's grace.
translations.idiomatic: Originally it meant recommending worthier men to repay imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 昔舜以禹為司空，禹拜稽首，讓於稷契及咎繇。

translations.literal: Formerly Shun made Yu Minister of Works—Yu bowed head—yielded to Ji Qi and Gao Yao.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun named Yu Minister of Works, Yu kowtowed and yielded to Ji, Qi, and Gao Yao.

sentences.zh: 使益為虞官，讓於硃虎、熊、羆。

translations.literal: Made Yi forest officer—yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi became superintendent of forests he yielded to Zhu Hu, Xiong, and Pi.

sentences.zh: 使伯夷典三禮，讓于夔龍。

translations.literal: Made Boyi oversee three rites—yielded to Kui Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyi took charge of ritual he yielded to Kui and Long.

sentences.zh: 唐虞之時，眾官初除，莫不皆讓也。

translations.literal: Tang Yu times—crowd of officials first appointed—none did not all yield.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yao and Shun every new minister yielded.

sentences.zh: 謝章之義，蓋取於此。

translations.literal: Gratitude memorial's meaning—probably taken from this.
translations.idiomatic: The gratitude memorial surely derives from this precedent.

sentences.zh: 《書》記之者，欲以永世作則。

translations.literal: Documents recorded it—desired thereby eternal generations take as model.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents preserved these acts as models for all ages.

sentences.zh: 季世所用，不賢不能讓賢，虛謝見用之恩而已。

translations.literal: Declining age's use—not worthy unable yield worthy—empty thank seeing-use grace only.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations hollowed it into empty thanks unless one were worthy enough to yield.

sentences.zh: 相承不變，習俗之失也。

translations.literal: Mutual inheritance unchanged—custom's error.
translations.idiomatic: Unchanging habit corrupted the rite.

sentences.zh: 夫敘用之官得通章表者，其讓賢推能乃通，其不能有所讓徒費簡紙者，皆絕不通。

translations.literal: As for narrative-employment officials able submit memorials—their yielding worthy pushing ability then passes—those unable to yield anything—only waste bamboo paper—all cut off not pass.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel officials may forward only memorials that nominate worthier men; empty paperwork is refused.

sentences.zh: 人臣初除，各思推賢能而讓之矣，讓之文付主者掌之。

translations.literal: Ministers first appointed—each thinks push worthy able and yield—yield document deliver holder manage.
translations.idiomatic: Every new appointee must propose a worthier substitute; the nominating text stays on file.

sentences.zh: 三司有缺，擇三司所讓最多者而用之。

translations.literal: Three Ducal offices vacant—select among three ducal yields most and use.
translations.idiomatic: When a Three Ducal seat opens, pick the candidate whom the three dukes most often yielded to.

sentences.zh: 此為一公缺，三公已豫選之矣。

translations.literal: This is one duke vacant—three dukes already beforehand selected.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one vacancy yields three advance nominees.

sentences.zh: 且主選之吏，不必任公而選三公，不如令三公自共選一公為詳也。

translations.literal: Moreover masters of selection clerks—need not appoint duke to select three dukes—better order three dukes themselves jointly select one duke—more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Better than letting personnel pick dukes is to let the three dukes jointly fill one seat—that yields finer judgment.

sentences.zh: 四征缺，擇四征所讓最多而用之，此為一征缺，四征已豫選之矣，必詳於停缺而令主者選四征也。

translations.literal: Four Expeditions vacant—select among four expeditions yielded most and use—this is one expedition vacant—four expeditions already beforehand selected—must more detailed than stopping vacancy ordering holder select four expeditions.
translations.idiomatic: Apply the same rule to the four expedition generals: let them nominate among themselves rather than leaving posts frozen while clerks guess.

sentences.zh: 尚書缺，擇尚書所讓最多者而用之，此為八尚書共選一尚書，詳于臨缺令主者選八尚書也。

translations.literal: Masters of Writing vacant—select among Masters of Writing yielded most and use—this is eight Masters of Writing jointly select one Master of Writing—more detailed than facing vacancy ordering holder select eight Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When a Masters of Writing post opens, choose from nominees whom serving ministers most endorsed—better than freezing eight seats while clerks decide.

sentences.zh: 郡守缺，擇眾郡所讓最多者而用之，詳于任主者令選百郡守也。

translations.literal: Commandery governor vacant—select among crowd commanderies yielded most—more detailed than appointing holder ordering select hundred commandery governors.
translations.idiomatic: For governors, pick from empire-wide endorsements rather than letting one clerk choose among hundreds.

sentences.zh: 夫以眾官百郡之讓，與主者共相比，不可同歲而論也。

translations.literal: Using crowd officials hundred commanderies' yields compared with holder together—cannot same year discuss.
translations.idiomatic: Collective judgment across counties outweighs a single clerk's opinion—it is not comparable.

sentences.zh: 雖復令三府參舉官，本不委以舉選之任，各不能以根其心也。

translations.literal: Though again order three bureaus jointly recommend officials—originally not entrust recommendation-selection duty—each cannot plant roots in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Even three bureaus nominating together lack full stake—they cannot commit wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 其所用心者裁之不二三，但令主者案官次而舉之，不用精也。

translations.literal: What they use heart on trims not two three—but order holder examine office order and raise—not using refinement.
translations.idiomatic: They skim candidates and leave personnel to promote by roster—no refinement.

sentences.zh: 賢愚皆讓，百姓耳目盡為國耳目。

translations.literal: Worthy and foolish all yield—commoners' ears eyes wholly become state's ears eyes.
translations.idiomatic: When everyone yields recommendations, the people become the ruler's eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 夫人情爭則欲毀己所不知，讓則競推於勝己。

translations.literal: As for human feeling—contend then desire destroy what self does not know—yield then compete push to surpass self.
translations.idiomatic: Rivalry breeds slander of unknown rivals; yielding urges promotion of betters.

sentences.zh: 故世爭則毀譽交錯，優劣不分，難得而讓也。

translations.literal: Therefore age contends then destroy praise crisscross—excellent inferior undistinguished—hard obtain and yield.
translations.idiomatic: Strife scrambles praise and blame until yielding is impossible.

sentences.zh: 時讓則賢智顯出，能否之美歷歷相次，不可得而亂也。

translations.literal: Age yields then worthy wise appears—able unable's beauty clear clear mutually ordered—cannot obtain and confuse.
translations.idiomatic: When yielding prevails, talent stands out in clear order—nothing confuses it.

sentences.zh: 當此時也，能退身修已者，讓之者多矣。

translations.literal: At this moment—those able withdraw body cultivate self—those yielding many.
translations.idiomatic: Then those who cultivate themselves attract many sponsors.

sentences.zh: 雖欲守貧賤，不可得也。

translations.literal: Though wish guard poverty lowliness—cannot obtain.
translations.idiomatic: They cannot stay obscure even if they wish.

sentences.zh: 馳騖進趣而欲人見讓，猶卻行而求前也。

translations.literal: Galloping advancement pursuit yet wish people see yield—like retreat walking yet seeking forward.
translations.idiomatic: Scheming for promotion while expecting others to yield you is like walking backward to advance.

sentences.zh: 夫如此，愚智咸知進身求通，非修之於己則無由矣。

translations.literal: If thus—foolish wise all know advancing self seeking passage—if not cultivate in self—there is no route.
translations.idiomatic: Then everyone sees that advancement requires self-cultivation—there is no other path.

sentences.zh: 游外求者，於此相隨而歸矣。

translations.literal: Those wandering outside seeking—here follow and return.
translations.idiomatic: Opportunists fade away.

sentences.zh: 浮聲虛論，不禁而自息矣。

translations.literal: Floating sounds empty discussions—not forbid yet self cease.
translations.idiomatic: Empty gossip dies without edicts.

sentences.zh: 人人無所用其心，任眾人之議，而天下自化矣。

translations.literal: Everyone nowhere uses their heart—entrust crowd's deliberations—and under Heaven self transforms.
translations.idiomatic: Rulers need not scheme—trust public consensus and the realm orders itself.

sentences.zh: 不言之化行，巍巍之美於此著矣。

translations.literal: Non-speaking transformation practiced—towering beauty here manifests.
translations.idiomatic: Silent transformation unfolds—great majesty appears.

sentences.zh: 讓可以致此，豈可不務之哉！

translations.literal: Yielding can cause this—how can not devote to it!
translations.idiomatic: Yielding achieves this—how can we neglect it?

sentences.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「范宣子之讓，其下皆讓。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Tradition says: "Fan Xuanzi's yielding—his subordinates all yielded.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Tradition says: "When Fan Xuanzi yielded, his subordinates yielded too."

sentences.zh: 欒黶雖汰，弗敢違也。

translations.literal: Luan Yan though extravagant—dared not disobey.
translations.idiomatic: Even the arrogant Luan Yan did not dare disobey.

sentences.zh: 晉國以平，數世賴之。

translations.literal: Jin state thereby pacified—several generations relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin regained peace and enjoyed stability for generations.

sentences.zh: 」上世之化也，君子尚能而讓其下，小人力農以事其上，上下有禮，讒慝遠黜，由不爭也。

translations.literal: Upper age's transformation—gentlemen esteemed able and yielded below—petty men strove in farming to serve above—above below had ritual—slander evil banished far—from not contending.
translations.idiomatic: In high antiquity gentlemen honored ability and yielded to juniors; commoners farmed to serve superiors; ritual ran above and below; slander vanished because none quarreled.

sentences.zh: 及其亂也，國家之弊，恆必由之。

translations.literal: Reaching its disorder—state's corruption—always must come from this.
translations.idiomatic: When order collapses, national ruin always stems from contention.

sentences.zh: 篤論了了如此。

translations.literal: Earnest discourse clear thus.
translations.idiomatic: Sound doctrine states it plainly.

sentences.zh: 在朝君子典選大官，能不以人廢言，舉而行之，各以讓賢舉能為先務，則群才猥出，能否殊別，蓋世之功，莫大於此。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen managing selection great officials—able not because person discard words—raise and practice—each take yielding worthy recommending able as first task—then crowd talents swarm out—able unable distinguished—age's accomplishment—none greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: If ministers who manage appointments heed this counsel and put recommending worthier men first, talent will multiply and ranks will sort themselves—no reform would surpass it.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，進爵為伯，累遷少府。

translations.literal: Taishi beginning—advanced noble to Earl—promoted repeatedly Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taishi he rose from baron to earl and eventually Privy Treasurer.

sentences.zh: 咸甯中為太常。

translations.literal: Xianning middle served Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianning he served as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書。

translations.literal: Transferred Master of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Master of Writing.

sentences.zh: 杜預之伐吳也，寔以本官行鎮南軍司。

translations.literal: When Du Yu campaigned against Wu—Shi in original office acted Guard South army clerk.
