translations.idiomatic: During Du Yu's conquest of Wu, Liu Shi served as army clerk to the Guard South command at his current rank.

sentences.zh: 初，寔妻盧氏生子躋而卒，華氏將以女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier—Shi's wife Lady Lu bore son Ji then died—Hua clan intended daughter marry him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi's wife Lady Lu bore Ji and died; the Hua family wished to marry him a daughter.

sentences.zh: 寔弟智諫曰：「華家類貪，必破門戶。

translations.literal: Shi's brother Zhi remonstrated: "Hua family sort greedy—surely will destroy household.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Liu Zhi warned: "The Huas are grasping and will ruin the family."

sentences.zh: 」辭之不得，竟婚華氏而生子夏。

translations.literal: Declining could not obtain—in the end married Hua clan and bore son Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to refuse, he married into the Huas and fathered Xia.

sentences.zh: 寔竟坐夏受賂，免官。

translations.literal: Shi in the end because Xia sat accepting bribes—dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi lost office when Xia took bribes.

sentences.zh: 頃之為大司農，又以夏罪免。

translations.literal: Shortly served Minister of Agriculture—again because Xia crime dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon restored as Minister of Agriculture, he was dismissed again over Xia's crimes.

sentences.zh: 寔每還州裏，鄉人載酒肉以候之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shi returned to village—villagers loaded wine meat to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Liu Shi visited home, villagers brought wine and meat to greet him.

sentences.zh: 寔難逆其意，輒共啖而返其餘。

translations.literal: Shi difficult oppose their intent—always together ate and returned remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Loath to refuse, he shared the meal and sent back what remained.

sentences.zh: 或謂寔曰：「君行高一世，而諸子不能遵。

translations.literal: Someone told Shi: "Your conduct high one age—yet sons cannot follow.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "Your integrity towers above the age, yet your sons do not follow it.

sentences.zh: 何不旦夕切磋，使知過而自改邪！

translations.literal: Why not dawn dusk grind polish—make know fault and self correct!
translations.idiomatic: Why not instruct them daily until they mend their faults?

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「吾之所行，是所聞見，不相祖習，豈復教誨之所得乎！

translations.literal: Shi said: "What I practice—is what I heard saw—not mutually inherited habit—how again instruction obtains!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi replied: "What I follow comes from what I saw and heard—it was not handed down by habit; lectures cannot replicate that."

sentences.zh: 」世以寔言為當。

translations.literal: Age considered Shi's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: People judged his reply sound.

sentences.zh: 後起為國子祭酒、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Later raised Libationer Imperial Academy—Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled as Libationer of the Imperial Academy and Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 湣懷太子初封廣陵王，高選師友，以寔為師。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Minhuai first enfeoffed Prince of Guangling—high selected teachers friends—made Shi teacher.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Minhuai was first invested as Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi was chosen as his tutor.

sentences.zh: 元康初，進爵為侯，累遷太子太保，加侍中、特進、右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，領冀州都督。

translations.literal: Yuankang beginning—advanced noble Marquis—promoted repeatedly Crown Prince Grand Guardian—added Palace Attendant—Exceptional Advance—Right Household Grandee—establishment equal Three Dukes—concurrently Ji Province commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuankang he advanced to marquis, rose to Crown Prince Grand Guardian, added Palace Attendant, Exceptional Advance, Right Household Grandee, establishment equal to the Three Dukes, and concurrent Ji Province commander.

sentences.zh: 九年，策拜司空，遷太保，轉太傅。

translations.literal: Ninth year—patent appointed Minister of Works—promoted Grand Guardian—transferred Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Minister of Works, then Grand Guardian, then Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 太安初，寔以老病遜位，賜安車駟馬、錢百萬，以侯就第。

translations.literal: Taian beginning—Shi because old illness yielded position—granted secure carriage four horses—million cash—take marquis go mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taian he resigned for age and illness, receiving a carriage, team, one million cash, and retired home as marquis.

sentences.zh: 及長沙成都之相攻也，寔為軍人所掠，潛歸鄉里。

translations.literal: When Changsha and Chengdu mutually attacked—Shi was army men plundered—secretly returned village.
translations.idiomatic: When the princes of Changsha and Chengdu fought, soldiers plundered Liu Shi, who slipped home.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔曰：「昔虞任五臣，致垂拱之化，漢相蕭何，興寧一之譽，故能光隆於當時，垂裕於百代。

translations.literal: Third year edict: "Formerly Yu employed five ministers—achieved draped-arms transformation—Han minister Xiao He—raised tranquil-oneness praise—therefore able glorify rise at age—hang surplus hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year an edict ran: "Ancient Yu employed five ministers and achieved effortless rule; Han Chancellor Xiao He won fame for securing unity—thus they shone in their day and blessed later ages.

sentences.zh: 朕紹天明命，臨御萬邦，所以崇顯政道者，亦賴之於元臣庶尹，畢力股肱，以副至望。

translations.literal: We inherit bright mandate—oversee myriad regions—therefore elevate manifest government Way—also relies on chief ministers many directors—exhaust strength arms legs—to match utmost hope.
translations.idiomatic: We have received Heaven's charge and rule all lands; exalted governance depends on chief ministers who serve as Our arms and legs to meet Our hopes.

sentences.zh: 而君年耆告老，確然難違。

translations.literal: Yet lord aged announces old—firmly cannot oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cite age and wish to retire—We cannot refuse resolutely.

sentences.zh: 今聽君以侯就第，位居三司之上，秩祿准舊，賜几杖不朝及宅一區。

translations.literal: Now We hear lord take marquis go mansion—rank position above Three Ducal—stipend salary standard old—grant stool staff not court and mansion one ward.
translations.idiomatic: We permit you to retire home as marquis with precedence above the Three Dukes, stipends as before, a stool and staff excusing court attendance, and one residence.

sentences.zh: 國之大政，將就諮於君，副朕意焉。

translations.literal: State's great policies—will near consult lord—match Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: We shall consult you on great affairs of state so Our wishes may be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 」歲余薨，時年九十一，諡曰元。

translations.literal: Over a year later he died—at the time age ninety-one—posthumous name Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died a little over a year later at ninety-one with the posthumous name Yuan ("Primary").

sentences.zh: 寔少貧窶，杖策徒行，每所憩止，不累主人，薪水之事，皆自營給。

translations.literal: Shi from youth was poor—staff whip walked on foot—each place rested—not burdening host—firewood and water matters—all self managed supply.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi grew up destitute, walking with a staff, and whenever he lodged he took nothing from hosts, gathering fuel and water himself.

sentences.zh: 及位望通顯，每崇儉素，不尚華麗。

translations.literal: Reaching position and renown thorough display—each honored frugal plain—not esteemed splendor and finery.
translations.idiomatic: After he rose to eminence he still favored plain simplicity over display.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣石崇家，如廁，見有絳紋帳，裀褥甚麗，兩婢持香囊。

translations.literal: Once he went to Shi Chong's house—entered toilet—saw crimson patterned curtains—cushions very beautiful—two maids held incense pouches.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting Shi Chong, he entered a lavatory hung with crimson brocade, fine cushions, and two maids holding sachets.

sentences.zh: 寔便退，笑謂崇曰：「誤入卿內。

translations.literal: Shi then withdrew—laughing said to Chong: "Mistakenly entered your inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi stepped back and said with a smile: "I blundered into your private rooms."

sentences.zh: 」崇曰：「是廁耳。

translations.literal: Chong said: "It is the toilet only.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chong said: "That is the privy."

sentences.zh: 」寔曰：「貧士未嘗得此。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Poor scholar never obtained this.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shi answered: "A poor scholar like me has never seen the like."

sentences.zh: 」乃更如他廁。

translations.literal: Thereupon again went to another toilet.
translations.idiomatic: He then used a different privy.

sentences.zh: 雖處榮寵，居無第宅，所得俸祿，贍恤親故。

translations.literal: Though located in glory and favor—dwelling without mansion—obtained stipend salary—supporting and relieving kin and old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Despite high rank he kept no grand house, spending his salary on kin and old friends.

sentences.zh: 雖禮教陵遲，而行己以正。

translations.literal: Though ritual teaching eroded—yet conducted self with rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Even as ritual declined he lived uprightly.

sentences.zh: 喪妻為廬杖之制，終喪不禦內。

translations.literal: Bereaved wife made hut and staff system—end mourning not approach inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning his wife he kept mourning hut and staff rites and avoided the inner chambers until the period ended.

sentences.zh: 輕薄者笑之，寔不以介意。

translations.literal: Frivolous persons laughed at him—Shi did not take it to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The shallow mocked him; Liu Shi ignored them.

sentences.zh: 自少及老，篤學不倦，雖居職務，卷弗離手。

translations.literal: From youth to old—diligent study not weary—though holding office—scrolls never left hand.
translations.idiomatic: From youth to age he studied tirelessly and never set a book aside even in office.

sentences.zh: 尤精《三傳》，辨正《公羊》，以為衛輒不應辭以王父命，祭仲失為臣之節，舉此二端以明臣子之體，遂行於世。

translations.literal: Especially refined Three Commentaries—rectified Gongyang—held that Wei Kuo should not decline citing grandfather's order—Jizhong lost subject's standard—raised these two ends to clarify subject-son's body—thereupon practiced in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Prince Zhe of Wei should not refuse office citing his grandfather's command and that Jizhong lacked the standard of a minister; these two examples clarified the duties of subject and son and won acceptance across the realm.

sentences.zh: 又撰《春秋條例》二十卷。

translations.literal: Also composed Chunqiu regulations twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote twenty fascicles of Chunqiu regulations.

sentences.zh: 有二子，躋、夏。

translations.literal: Had two sons—Ji and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Ji and Xia.

sentences.zh: 躋字景雲，官至散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Ji styled Jingyun—reached office Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, courtesy name Jingyun, rose to Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 夏以貪污棄放於世。

translations.literal: Xia by corruption was cast away in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xia was disgraced and cast out for corruption.

sentences.zh: 弟智，字子房，貞素有兄風。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhi styled Zifang—chaste plain had elder brother's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liu Zhi, courtesy name Zifang, shared his brother's integrity.

sentences.zh: 少貧窶，每負薪自給，讀誦不輟，竟以儒行稱。

translations.literal: From youth poor—each carried firewood self supply—read and recite not stop—in the end by Confucian conduct praised.
translations.idiomatic: He was poor in youth, carried firewood to live, never stopped reading, and was praised for Confucian conduct.

sentences.zh: 曆中書黃門吏部郎，出為潁川太守。

translations.literal: Served Palace Yellow Gates Personnel Director—went out as Yingchuan governor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Palace Bureau, at the Yellow Gates, and as Personnel Director, then became governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 平原管輅嘗謂人曰：「吾與劉潁川兄弟語，使人神思清發，昏不假寐。

translations.literal: Pingyuan Guan Lu once told people: "I with Liu Yingchuan brothers speak—makes people's spirit thought clear and rising—evening not borrow sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Lu of Pingyuan said: "Conversation with the Liu brothers of Yingchuan clears the mind; I need no nap by day."

sentences.zh: 自此之外，殆白日欲寢矣。

translations.literal: Outside this—almost daytime wishes to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: With anyone else I could nap all afternoon."

sentences.zh: 」入為秘書監，領南陽王師，加散騎常侍，遷侍中、尚書、太常。

translations.literal: Entered as Secretary Supervisor—concurrently Prince of Nanyang tutor—added Regular Palace Attendant—promoted Palace Attendant, Master of Writing, Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He became Secretary Supervisor, tutor to the Prince of Nanyang, Regular Palace Attendant, then Palace Attendant, Master of Writing, and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 著《喪服釋疑論》，多所辨明。

translations.literal: Composed Mourning Dress resolving doubts treatise—much clarified.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote "Treatise Clarifying Doubts on Mourning Dress," settling many questions.

sentences.zh: 太康末卒，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Taikang end died—posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of Taikang with the posthumous name Cheng.

sentences.zh: 高光，字宣茂，陳留圉城人，魏太尉柔之子也。

translations.literal: Gao Guang styled Xuanmao—Chenliu Yucheng person—Wei Grand Commandant Rou's son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Guang, courtesy name Xuanmao, was from Yucheng in Chenliu and son of Wei Grand Commandant Gao Rou.

sentences.zh: 光少習家業，明練刑理。

translations.literal: Guang from youth practiced family occupation—clear proficient in penal principle.
translations.idiomatic: He studied his family's legal tradition from youth and mastered penal doctrine.

sentences.zh: 初以太子舍人累遷尚書郎，出為幽州刺史、潁州太守。

translations.literal: First as crown prince attendant promoted repeatedly Master of Writing Gentleman—went out Inspector Youzhou—Yingzhou governor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as crown prince attendant, rose to Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, then served as Inspector of Youzhou and governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時武帝置黃沙獄，以典詔囚。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Wu established Yellow Sand prison—to administer edict prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu then founded the Yellow Sand prison for imperial-order cases.

sentences.zh: 以光曆世明法，用為黃沙御史，秩與中丞同，遷廷尉。

translations.literal: Because Guang generations clarified law—used as Yellow Sand Imperial Clerk—rank same Assistant Clerk—promoted Director of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For his family's legal expertise he became Yellow Sand Imperial Clerk with rank equal to the Palace Assistant Clerk, then Director of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元康中，拜尚書，典三公曹。

translations.literal: Yuankang middle appointed Master of Writing—managed Three Ducal bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang he became Master of Writing and headed the Three Ducal bureau.

sentences.zh: 時趙王倫篡逆，光於其際，守道全貞。

translations.literal: At time Prince Zhao Lun usurped rebellion—Guang at that juncture—guarded Way preserved purity.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhao Lun usurped the throne, Gao Guang kept faith and integrity.

sentences.zh: 及倫賜死，齊王冏輔政，復以光為廷尉，遷尚書，加奉車都尉。

translations.literal: When Lun granted death—Prince of Qi Jiong assisted governance—again made Guang Director of Justice—promoted Master of Writing—added Colonel Chariot Command.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun was forced to die, Prince of Qi Sima Jiong took charge and reappointed Gao Guang Director of Justice, then Master of Writing with the additional title Colonel of Chariots.

sentences.zh: 後從駕討成都王穎有勳，封延陵縣公，邑千八百戶。

translations.literal: Later followed imperial carriage campaigned Prince Chengdu Ying had merit—enfeoffed Duke of Yanling—estate thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He later accompanied the emperor against Prince Chengdu Sima Ying and earned merit, receiving the rank Duke of Yanling with eighteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 于時朝廷咸推光明于用法，故頻典理官。

translations.literal: At that time court all pushed Guang clarity in applying law—therefore repeatedly directed judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The court praised his clarity in applying law and repeatedly placed him over justice posts.

sentences.zh: 惠帝為張方所逼，幸長安，朝臣奔散，莫有從者，光獨侍帝而西。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui by Zhang Fang compelled—visited Chang'an—court ministers fled scattered—none followed—Guang alone attended emperor west.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was driven by Zhang Fang to Chang'an and ministers fled, only Gao Guang accompanied him west.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Promoted Left Vice Director Master of Writing—added Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 光兄誕為上官巳等所用，曆徐、雍二州刺史。

translations.literal: Guang elder brother Dan employed by Shangguan Si et al.—served Xu and Yong two prefectures inspectors.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dan worked for Shangguan Si and successively governed Xu and Yong.

sentences.zh: 誕性任放無倫次，而決烈過人，與光異操。

translations.literal: Dan nature unrestrained without order—yet decisive fierce surpassed others—with Guang different conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dan was reckless and undisciplined yet bolder than most—a temper unlike his brother.

sentences.zh: 常謂光小節，恆輕侮之，光事誕愈謹。

translations.literal: Often called Guang petty matters—always lightly insulted him—Guang served Dan more careful.
translations.idiomatic: He sneered at Gao Guang's caution, yet Guang treated him with increasing respect.

sentences.zh: 帝既還洛陽，時太弟新立，重選傅訓，以光為少傅，加光祿大夫，常侍如故。

translations.literal: Emperor after returning Luoyang—at time Grand Heir newly established—heavy selected tutor instruction—made Guang Junior Tutor—added Household Grandee—regular attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang and the heir apparent was newly installed, tutors were chosen carefully; Gao Guang became Junior Tutor with Household Grandee and continued as Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝即位，加光祿大夫金章紫綬，與傅祗並見推崇。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—added Household Grandee gold seal purple ribbon—with Fu Zhi together seen esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai took the throne, Gao Guang received Household Grandee with gold seal and purple ribbon alongside Fu Zhi in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 尋為尚書令，本官如故。

translations.literal: Soon Master of Writing Director—original office as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became Director of the Masters of Writing while keeping prior duties.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，贈司空、侍中。

translations.literal: By illness died—posthumously gifted Minister of Works—Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously honored as Minister of Works and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 屬京洛傾覆，竟未加諡。

translations.literal: Because Luoyang overturned—in the end not added posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of Luoyang prevented conferral of a posthumous name.

sentences.zh: 子韜字子遠，放佚無檢。

translations.literal: Son Tao styled Ziyuan—dissolute without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Tao, courtesy name Ziyuan, was dissolute and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 光為廷尉時，韜受貨賕，有司奏案之，而光不知。

translations.literal: When Guang Director of Justice—Tao accepted goods bribes—officials memorial impeached—yet Guang did not know.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Guang headed the Court of Justice, Tao took bribes; authorities impeached him but Guang knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 時人雖非光不能防閑其子，以其用心有素，不以為累。

translations.literal: People of time though blamed Guang could not fence son—because his intent longstanding—not regarded as stain.
translations.idiomatic: Critics faulted him for not controlling his son, yet his lifelong integrity spared him lasting blame.

sentences.zh: 初，光詣長安留台，以韜兼右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Earlier Guang went Chang'an provisional court—made Tao concurrent Right Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gao Guang attended the provisional court at Chang'an, he named Tao concurrent Right Guard general.

sentences.zh: 韜與殿省小人交通，及光卒，仍於喪中往來不絕。

translations.literal: Tao communicated with palace petty persons—and Guang died—still during mourning came went without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Tao consorted with palace underlings and, after Guang died, continued those visits even in mourning.

sentences.zh: 時東海王越輔政，不朝觀。

translations.literal: At time Prince Donghai Yue assisted governance—not court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Donghai Sima Yue held power but skipped court audiences.

sentences.zh: 韜知人心有望，密與太傅參軍薑賾、京兆杜概等謀討越，事泄伏誅。

translations.literal: Tao knew people's hearts had hopes—secretly with Grand Tutor aide Jiang Ze—Jingzhao Du Gai et al. plotted attack Yue—matter leaked executed.
translations.idiomatic: Reading popular resentment, Tao secretly joined Grand Tutor aide Jiang Ze and Du Gai of Jingzhao to move against Yue; the plot leaked and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：下士競而文，中庸靜而質，不若進不足而退有餘也。

translations.literal: Historians say: inferior scholars contend yet ornate—middle path tranquil yet plain—not like advancing insufficient yet retreating surplus.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: petty scholars strive for polish; the moderate stay plain—it is better to advance modestly and retire amply.

sentences.zh: 魏舒、劉寔發慮精華，結綬登槐，覽止成務。

translations.literal: Wei Shu Liu Shi emitted thought essence—tied ribbons ascended locust—overview stop accomplish affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shu and Liu Shi distilled keen insight, entered high office, grasped essentials, and delivered results.

sentences.zh: 季和切問近對，當官正色。

translations.literal: Jihe incisive question near answer—holding office stern demeanor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xi answered probing questions plainly and faced duty with a stern air.

sentences.zh: 詩云「貪人敗類」，豈劉夏之謂歟！

translations.literal: Odes says "greedy men ruin kind"—surely refers to Liu Xia!
translations.idiomatic: The Odes says "greedy men ruin their kin"—did it mean Liu Xia?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：舒言不矜，憙對千乘。

translations.literal: Praise says: Shu speaks not boast—Xi faces thousand chariots.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Wei Shu spoke without arrogance; Li Xi answered princes to their faces.

sentences.zh: 子真、宣茂，雅志難陵。

translations.literal: Zizhen Xuanmao—elegant intent hard eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zizhen and Gao Xuanmao pursued lofty aims none could eclipse.

sentences.zh: 進忠能舉，退讓攸興。

translations.literal: Advancing loyalty able recommending—retreating yielding thereby rises.
translations.idiomatic: They advanced loyal talent and welcomed yielding when stepping back.

sentences.zh: 皎皎瑚器，來光玉繩。

translations.literal: Bright bright coral vessel—come shine jade cord.
translations.idiomatic: Bright as coral vessels, they brought luster like stars along the Jade Cord.
